question: What was the average price of a Big Mac in the United States in July 2024, according to The Economist's Big Mac index?
source_title: The Economist - Big Mac index data (big-mac-raw-index.csv, USA, 2024-07-01)
explainer: The Economist has tracked burger prices since 1986 as a light-hearted guide to currency values. The US Big Mac passed $6 in 2025.

question: What was the UK National Living Wage per hour for workers aged 21 and over from April 2024?
source_title: Business Wales - National Minimum Wage and National Living Wage rates 2024
explainer: The 9.8% rise from £10.42 was the largest cash increase ever, and the age threshold dropped from 23 to 21. A 37.5-hour week at this rate pays about £430.

question: At what price per share did Apple sell its stock in its initial public offering on 12 December 1980?
source_title: TechCrunch - A look back in IPO: Apple, the early PC purveyor
explainer: The 4.6 million shares raised about $100 million and valued Apple near $1.8 billion by the close of its first day. Thanks to five splits, one of those $22 shares is now 224 shares.

question: How many cents did a US First-Class Forever stamp cost after the price rise of 14 July 2024?
source_title: CBS News - Stamp prices poised to rise again, for the 2nd time this year
explainer: It was the second increase of 2024, up from 68 cents in January. A first-class stamp cost 20 cents in 1981.

question: What was the advertised price of the cheapest Ford Model T, the two-seat Runabout, in the United States in 1925?
source_title: Humboldt State University Special Collections - Price of a Ford (1925 listing)
explainer: That was the lowest price ever for a new mass-market car in the US, roughly $4,700 in today's money. The same Runabout had cost around $900 in 1910.

question: How many billionaires were on Forbes' 2024 list of the world's billionaires?
source_title: Forbes - The World's Billionaires 2024 (as reported by AP)
explainer: A record, with 813 of them in the US. Their combined wealth of $14.2 trillion exceeded the GDP of every country except the US and China.

question: What was the world's GDP per person in 2023, in current US dollars (World Bank)?
source_title: FRED / World Bank - Gross Domestic Product Per Capita for World (NYGDPPCAPCDWLD)
explainer: Roughly $107 trillion of output shared among 8 billion people. The US figure is about six times this; India's is about a fifth of it.

question: What was the median US household income in 2023, according to the Census Bureau?
source_title: US Census Bureau - Income in the United States: 2023 (P60-282)
explainer: Up 4% in real terms from 2022, the first significant rise since 2019. Half of US households earned more than this and half earned less.

question: What was Luxembourg's GDP per person in 2023, in current US dollars (World Bank)?
source_title: FRED / World Bank - Gross Domestic Product Per Capita for Luxembourg (PCAGDPLUA646NWDB)
explainer: The highest of any country. The figure is inflated because over 200,000 cross-border commuters add to GDP but not to the resident population of about 670,000.

question: What is the annual salary of the President of the United States, as set by law since 2001?
source_title: 3 U.S. Code § 102 - Compensation of the President (govinfo)
explainer: Doubled from $200,000 in 2001, plus a $50,000 expense allowance. Inflation has since eroded the salary's buying power by roughly 40%.

question: How much did the United States pay Russia for Alaska in 1867?
source_title: Wikipedia - Alaska Purchase
explainer: About two cents an acre for 586,000 square miles, roughly $130 million in today's dollars. Critics mocked the deal as 'Seward's Folly'.

question: How much money, in Swedish kronor, came with each full Nobel Prize awarded in 2023?
source_title: NobelPrize.org - The Nobel Prize amounts
explainer: Up from 10 million kronor the year before, worth about US$1 million at 2023 exchange rates. A prize shared by three laureates is split between them.

question: What was the GDP of Tuvalu, the Pacific island nation of about 10,000 people, in 2023 in US dollars?
source_title: FRED / World Bank - Gross Domestic Product for Tuvalu (MKTGDPTVA646NWDB)
explainer: One of the smallest economies on Earth, smaller than many single shopping malls. A notable slice of its income comes from leasing its '.tv' internet domain and selling fishing licences.

question: What price, including fees, did Leonardo da Vinci's Salvator Mundi fetch at Christie's in New York in November 2017?
source_title: WAMC/NPR - Leonardo da Vinci portrait of Christ sells for record-shattering $450 million
explainer: Still the most expensive artwork ever sold at auction, more than double the previous record. The same painting sold for £45 in 1958 when it was thought to be a copy.

question: What was the advertised jackpot of the record US Powerball lottery draw won in California in November 2022?
source_title: Powerball.com - Ticket in California wins world record $2.04 billion Powerball jackpot
explainer: That is the annuity value; the lump-sum option was $997.6 million before tax. The jackpot had rolled over for three months at odds of 1 in 292 million.

question: What was the United Nations' approved regular budget for the year 2024?
source_title: IISD SDG Knowledge Hub - Member States Approve USD 3.59 Billion UN Budget for 2024
explainer: About 45 cents per person on Earth, and less than New York City spends in two weeks. Peacekeeping is funded separately at roughly $6 billion a year.

question: How much funding did the US Congress give NASA for fiscal year 2024?
source_title: The Planetary Society - NASA's FY 2024 Budget
explainer: About 0.4% of federal spending, and NASA's first year-on-year cut since 2013. At its 1960s Apollo peak NASA took more than 4% of the federal budget.

question: What was the total worldwide cinema box office in 2023, in US dollars?
source_title: Gower Street Analytics - 2023 global box office estimated at $33.9 billion
explainer: Up 31% on 2022 thanks to Barbie, Oppenheimer and Super Mario, but still 15% below the pre-pandemic average. North America made up about $9 billion.

question: How much did the world's governments spend on their militaries in 2023, according to SIPRI?
source_title: SIPRI - Trends in World Military Expenditure, 2023
explainer: A record, equal to 2.3% of world GDP or $306 per person on Earth. The US alone accounted for $916 billion, about 37% of the total.

question: What was India's GDP in 2023, in current US dollars (World Bank)?
source_title: FRED / World Bank - Gross Domestic Product for India (MKTGDPINA646NWDB)
explainer: The fifth-largest economy in the world, behind the US, China, Germany and Japan. Spread over 1.4 billion people, that is only about $2,500 per person.

question: How much did the US federal government spend in total in fiscal year 2023 (October 2022 to September 2023)?
source_title: US Treasury - Combined Statement of Receipts, Outlays, and Balances FY2023: Outlays
explainer: Around $18,000 per US resident. Receipts were $4.4 trillion, leaving a $1.7 trillion deficit; Social Security and interest on the debt alone topped $2 trillion.

question: What was the gross national debt of the United States on 31 December 2024?
source_title: US Treasury - Monthly Statement of the Public Debt, December 2024
explainer: About $106,000 per US resident and growing by roughly $2 trillion a year. The debt first crossed $36 trillion in November 2024, only four months after passing $35 trillion.

question: What was the total GDP of the whole world in 2023, in current US dollars (World Bank)?
source_title: FRED / World Bank - Gross Domestic Product for World (NYGDPMKTPCDWLD)
explainer: The US made up roughly a quarter of it and China about a sixth. The whole world economy was only about $34 trillion in 2000.
